_comment: PLAT-35 — THE PINNED CORPUS. WHAT MAKES A SHIFTED CORPUS REDDEN.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.
ALL EIGHT layout questions carry a filed gap, so ALL FORTY-EIGHT tier-3
cells in `test_cross_renderer_visual_alignment.nim` take the
`residualHolds` branch. What those forty-eight assert is that EIGHT NAMED
divergences have not grown past their filed shapes. That is a real claim.
It is not the claim 'the two front-ends agree'. The `gaps.len == 0`
branch — the alignment claim itself — is NOT REACHABLE by any cell.
That count was SEVEN for one day and the day is worth recording. On
2026-09-21 `PLAT35-VG7` was retired because the morning's run showed both
arms answering an EMPTY `inline-value-runs-by-line` set, which made six
cells take the alignment branch — live, and vacuous, since two empty
answers compare equal. Re-running the same binary on the same tree six
times showed FIVE runs reporting the GPUI values and one not: the gap had
been retired against the minority run. It is re-filed as `PLAT35-VG9`,
the intermittency is `PLAT35-PD3`, and no cell is on the alignment branch
again. None of the residuals below changed; what changed is that the
suite now asserts the GPUI locals ARRIVED rather than merely that nothing
raised while fetching them.
The consequence was measured on 2026-09-21: the gate was re-run against a
corpus in which FOUR OF SIX scenarios had reached a different program
state, and it stayed GREEN at 90 cases and 309 assertions. The residual
for `gutter-marks-by-line` compares mark KINDS as a sorted multiset —
both sides said `execution`, so it held — and never looks at the line.
The residual for `which-panes-are-present` asks only that `editor`,
`state` and `calltrace` appear on both sides. Neither can see a corpus
move, and nothing else in the suite was reading these numbers at all.
So the numbers the findings rest on are PINNED here and compared. A
re-run that lands somewhere else now fails by name, with both figures in
the message, instead of being absorbed by a residual that was describing
a different property.
WHY THESE THREE MEASUREMENTS AND NOT OTHERS.
* THE STOPPED LINE is what `PLAT35-VG6` is entirely a claim about, and
it is the single number an operation that lands in the wrong place
moves. It is read back out of each front-end's own
`gutter-marks-by-line` answer by `executionLineIn`, so both arms are
read by ONE function over the data the gate already compares — not by
two extractors that could disagree about what they mean.
* THE PANE CENSUS is what `PLAT35-VG5`'s four-against-eight is a claim
about. A front-end that stopped drawing four of its panes would still
satisfy that question's residual.
* THE EDITOR ROW COUNT, WHICH THIS FILE WAS BLIND TO, AND THAT BLINDNESS
IS HOW A DRIFT SURVIVED THE MECHANISM BUILT TO CATCH ONE. Measured
2026-09-21: `returned-calltrace`'s Electron answer flipped between
`rows=36;first=82;last=117` and `rows=35;first=83;last=117` across runs
of the identical specification — four and three of seven captures. The
two pins above cannot see a scrolled editor, and `editor-row-count`'s
own residual (it carries `PLAT35-VG2`) asks only that both sides drew
rows numbered ascending from a real line. The capture is repaired; this
is what makes the NEXT one visible.
THE WHOLE ANSWER STRING IS PINNED, not the count alone: `first` and
`last` are what say which window the editor holds, and a scroll that
moved the window while keeping the count is exactly what a bare count
would absorb.
THIS FILE NAMES RENDERERS AND `scenarios.json` DOES NOT. That is why it is
a separate file: the scenario definition names a recording, an operation
sequence, a viewport and a view, and naming a front-end in it would make
one definition into two. A pin is a measurement OF a front-end and belongs
with the other measurements.
WHEN A PIN CHANGES, THAT IS A DELIBERATE EDIT AND THE POINT. If a product
change moves where a front-end stops, this file is where somebody has to
say so, in the same commit, with the new number visible in the diff.

entry-shell._why: Not stepped. The session sits at its entry point, line 1.

stepped-editor._why: Six step-ins. Measured 2026-09-21, FIVE identical runs (the trajectory, the tick count, the operations moved, the settle attempts and the tier-1 verdict are byte-identical in all five): ticks 1..6 visit lines 1, 2, 29, 34, 39, 44, so the stop is line 44 — `calc`'s `def div` — and every one of those six is a module-level `def` statement.

advanced-state._why: Six step-ins and three nexts: 44 -> 54 -> 55 -> 56, the entries of the OPERATIONS dispatch table.

returned-calltrace._why: Twenty-one step-ins reach `evaluate` TWO frames deep (step 17 enters `main`, step 21 enters `evaluate`); the step-out returns to `main` at line 110, tick 37. Stepping out one frame shallower lands on line 113 at tick 171, which is byte-identical to where `continueForward` lands — that collision is what the previous three-operation spelling produced once the capture began asserting effect.
returned-calltrace._whyEditorRowsIsASet: THE EDITOR IS BOTTOM-ANCHORED HERE, which is the only place `PLAT35-PD4` can act. Measured 2026-09-21 at the 798px editor height: the resting scroll is 1788 (= 2574 + 12 - 798, the bound before the flow overlay's 21px view zone is counted) in 9 of 9 captures taken after the per-move frame settle landed, and was 1809 (= 2607 - 798, the bound with it) in 3 of 7 taken before. BOTH ARE PINNED rather than only the current one: PD4 is unfixed, the settle reduces its probability rather than removing it, and a pin that depends on a probability is a pin that flakes on a slower machine — in a lane shared with eleven other milestones. Tighten this to one member on the day PD4 is closed.

continued-event-log._why: Run forward to completion: line 113, tick 171, the last statement of `main`.
continued-event-log._whyEditorRowsIsASet: THE EDITOR IS BOTTOM-ANCHORED HERE TOO, and this is the scenario `PLAT35-PD4` was measured on: ONE operation, so a settle between operations has nothing to work with. At the 978px editor height the three bounds are 1596 (= 2574 - 978), 1608 (= 2586 - 978, the horizontal scrollbar counted) and 1629 (= 2607 - 978, the 21px view zone counted too), which put the first rendered line at 73, 74 and 75. ALL THREE WERE OBSERVED, in ten captures. They are not a list somebody collected: each is the arithmetic consequence of one content-height stage, so a corpus that moves — a different line, a different file, a different viewport — leaves the set entirely.

breakpoint-editor._why: Six step-ins, then a gutter mark. The mark does NOT move the program, which the capture asserts: the stop stays at line 44, tick 6, exactly `stepped-editor`'s, and the two scenarios are told apart by the breakpoint and by the viewport.
